question: Do diagnosis-before-mutation and context-bound mutation credit reduce wrong-layer or harmful self-repairs at matched known-world scope, before any external-agent claim?

diagnosis.decision_voi_internal_loss: wrong-layer indicator + probe cost; used only to choose a probe, never as the reported scientific scalar
diagnosis.hard_rule: No cost or correct-repair gain compensates a higher registered harmful-mutation rate when comparing RAKL control admission.

contextual_credit.transport_rule: Only same-family train->fresh transport is registered; no cross-family transfer.

MEASURED: arm differences in diagnosis outcome/cost vector over seeded worlds
arm differences in fresh-context operator choice/effect/regret
CONFORMANCE: renamed context has identical canonical digest
invalid candidate is removed before Pareto

terminal_rule.CONTROL_VALUE_SUPPORTED: DECISION_VOI has no greater harmful-mutation rate than every non-oracle diagnosis parent, lower wrong-layer rate than INFO_GAIN_PER_COST and FIXED_SURFACE, and total cost below MUTATE_ALL_PLAUSIBLE; CONTEXT_TRANSPORT_CREDIT has lower harmful-repair rate and lower regret than GLOBAL_CREDIT on fresh contexts.
terminal_rule.SIMPLER_PARENT_SUFFICIENT: A simpler diagnosis parent matches or dominates DECISION_VOI on the registered vector, or global credit matches contextual transport on fresh contexts.
terminal_rule.CONTROL_TRADEOFF_UNRESOLVED: No registered arm dominates under the hard-harm rule and vector comparison.
